newsitem.title: USA: Dlr ends lower in US as profit-taking stunts rally.
newsitem.headline: Dlr ends lower in US as profit-taking stunts rally.

text.p: The dollar shuffled lower in U.S. trade as profit-takers ended its latest rally to multi-year highs overnight, dealers said.
Rumors swirled that Germany would soon allow its official interest rates to rise, pushing the dollar off its lofty perch despite broad dollar bullishness, dealers said.

"The market made some new highs, but then it took a breather. I expect we'll continue to see new highs made throughout the rest of the week," said Rick Gomes, a managing director of foreign exchange at Republic National Bank of New York.

The greenback overnight marched to its highest level in nearly eight years against the German mark and rallied against other European currencies amid growing expectations that interest rates will soon rise in the United States.
The dollar also hit a four-year high against the Swiss franc, an eight-year peak versus the French franc and a nearly 12-year high against the Italian lira in early trade.
The dollar ended lower at 1.8655/65 marks versus 1.8685/95 at the open and an overnight high of 1.8730, its highest since October 1989. Dollar/yen fell to 118.28/38 from 118.57/67 at the open.

Against the Swiss franc, the dollar ended lower at 1.5248/53 versus 1.5305/15 at the open and an overnight peak of 1.5356. The dollar fell to 6.2935/65 French francs from 6.3070/00 at the open after peaking at 6.3137 overnight.
Currency traders cited residual interest to buy dollars after a pair of reports last Friday showed signs of vigor in the U.S. manufacturing sector and rapid U.S. job growth.

The U.S. Labor Department on Friday reported unemployment in July fell to a 24-year low while the National Association of Purchasing Management said its manufacturing index rose to its highest point since November 1994.
Signs of increasing U.S. economic vigor have boosted expectations that the Federal Reserve may raise interest rates later this year, which would tend to enhance the value of the dollar.

But the greenback began to surrender its gains by the start of New York trading amid rumors that the Bundesbank would let its repo rate float freely. Dealers said the market would push the rate higher if it were floated.
The Bundesbank set a fixed rate at its council meeting two weeks ago, but left open the possibility of floating the rate starting on Tuesday.
"All the talk about higher German interest rates was holding back the buck and making the mark stronger on the crosses," said Jay Wertheimer, senior foreign exchange trader at Banco di Sicilia.

Yet the prevailing economic weakness in Germany and the rest of continental Europe has stopped European central banks from raising rates for many months. Dealers said the Bundesbank would likely hold off until signs of growth appeared.

"We hear rumors about German rates going up every time the dollar is getting too high and the mark too weak, but there is no room to raise interest rates in Europe right now," said John Hanley, chief dealer at Bank Austria.
Germany will provide an important glimpse of its current economic status on Wednesday when it releases its employment report for the month of July.

In other trade the dollar fell to Canadian $1.3785/90 from C$1.3792/97. The British pound rose to $1.6311/18 from $1.6282/92. The Australian dollar rose to $0.7404/09 from $0.7387/92. ((--Chris Stetkiewicz, 212-859-1664))
